## Expression on this line

Emotional-interpersonal at Order 7 is **systematic emotional design**: the deliberate
construction of emotional systems based on explicit principles. "I design this emotional
environment because I have reasoned about it" — emotional design is self-authored rather
than inherited. The psychologist who constructs a systematic emotional intelligence
curriculum, the therapist who designs a treatment protocol, the leader who designs an
emotionally supportive culture — these are Stage 9 emotional architects.

The key advance from Stage 8 is **systemic emotional modeling**. The agent does not just
see multiple perspectives on emotion — it sees how emotional processes interact as a
dynamic system with feedback loops, emergent properties, and structural constraints.

Emotion at Stage 9 is understood as **designable**. The agent believes that emotional
intelligence can be intentionally improved through rational analysis and systematic design.
This is the modernist emotional psychology: emotions are engineering problems that can
be solved with the right design.

But emotional reasoning at Stage 9 is still **framework-bound**. The agent designs
emotional systems within a particular framework (cognitive-behavioral, psychodynamic,
humanistic) but cannot step outside the framework to evaluate it.

The transition from Stage 9 to Stage 10 occurs when the agent can evaluate entire
emotional frameworks.

In human development, Stage 9 corresponds to the professional who can construct and
defend a systematic emotional theory.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Institutional emotional design culture emerges. Universities, therapy
  institutes, emotional intelligence research centers.

- **UR:** The individual agent can construct and evaluate emotional systems using
  explicit principles.

- **LL:** Systemic emotional institutions emerge: therapy modalities, emotional
  education programs, emotional research centers.

- **LR:** The therapy room, the emotional intelligence curriculum, the research
  institute.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Methodological hubris — the belief that one's emotional approach
  is objectively true and all others are wrong.

- **Dark allergy:** Anti-psychological nihilism — the rejection of all systematic
  emotional reasoning.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to systematic emotional reasoning as the only valid
  approach.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting systematic emotion as dehumanizing.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Systemic emotional modeling:** The agent can trace emotional dynamics and predict
  how changes affect emotional outcomes.

- **Design-based emotional reasoning:** The agent proposes emotional improvements based
  on analysis.

- **Framework-bound analysis:** The agent reasons brilliantly within an emotional
  framework but cannot evaluate the framework itself.

- **Expert-dependent design:** Emotional design is concentrated in professionals.
